title: Tenant-aware QoS Prober and Acceptance Matrix for Dedicated Throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a tenant-aware load prober and deterministic acceptance matrix that validates Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees across mixed-tenant workloads and autoscaling policies. This ticket covers the harness design, tuning methodology to map synthetic load to production-equivalent token throughput, and formalized customer acceptance steps for enterprise sign-off. The output is a reproducible test run, a calibration artifact (mapping table from synthetic scenario to expected T/second), and an acceptance checklist templates for Solutions and Customer Success to use during onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration: synthetic scenarios map to historical customer traces within ±10% on mean token/s and within ±15% on 95th percentile latency when run on the same dedicated pool configuration.

QoS validation: under a nominated tenant-mix (see test matrix) the platform maintains configured throughput guarantees for P0 customers for 95% of test windows and does not violate safety limits for lower tiers.

Autoscaler safety: abrupt 3x inbound-sustained load spikes should trigger scaled capacity or graceful degradation policy within the configured SLO window (see rollout plan) and documented fallback behavior must be observed.

Reproducible artifacts: a single CLI invocation in the repo produces identical benchmark results given the same seed, and artifacts are stored in S3 with metadata tags for Git SHA, runtime image, and hardware profile.
Customer acceptance script: runbook validated with Solutions Engineering on two pilot customers and signoff captured as a signed checklist entry in the ticket.
No security findings: pass the security review for load generator credentials and RBAC interactions (security review ticket attached).
test_matrix: Tenant mixes: single-tenant heavy (90% P0), balanced multi-tenant (30/30/40), long-tail many small tenants (100 tenants churn model)
Prompt lengths: short (16–64 tokens), medium (128–512), long (512–4096)
Model variants: base FP16, int8-quantized and fallback-compatible smaller variant
Arrival patterns: steady-state uniform, poisson burst, scheduled ramp-and-sustain, on-demand spike (step increase)
KV/cache hit patterns: warm cache vs cold cache scenarios
metrics_to_collect: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (generation start to final token emitted)
GPU utilization and kernel-level stall indicators
cost estimate meter: estimated per-token cost during run
load_generator_config: Implementation: new tenant-aware prober in tools/load-prober (Go) using probabilistic arrival generators and token-equivalent workload estimator
Knobs: tenant_weight_distribution JSON, arrival_pattern=(poisson|constant|ramp), seed, concurrency_limit_per_tenant
Calibration mode: replay-mode that reads encrypted customer traces from s3://redwood-prod-traces and generates a mapping table to synthetic knobs
Safety: will respect per-tenant QPS caps and uses a sandbox routing tag to avoid impacting production pools
Observability: emits structured events compatible with Console ingest and links run-id to Grafana dashboard tags
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: initial prototype of probabilistic arrival generator merged (PR #1423) — basic single-tenant steady-state scenarios validated against internal microbenchmarks.

2026-02-27: added tenant-weight distribution and seed determinism; discovered 12% mismatch on token mapping vs production traces for long prompts; opened follow-up to improve token-estimator heuristics (ENG-86611).

2026-03-03: autoscaler instrumentation added; scale events now correlate with queue_length metric in synthetic runs. Observed lag in scale-up under poisson bursts — temporary mitigations added to policy (increase aggressiveness) pending further tuning.

2026-03-09: ran pilot with Solutions on 'AcmeChat' using a balanced multi-tenant scenario; validated acceptance script steps and captured signed checklist items. Two follow-up items recorded in review_feedback.
2026-03-12: prepared reproducible run CLI and uploaded calibration artifacts to S3; ready for security review handoff.
decisions: Use probabilistic arrival model (Poisson) for primary benchmark to reflect real-world burstiness; include constant-rate baseline for capacity comparisons.
Express throughput guarantees as token-equivalent throughput and percentile violation budget rather than raw request-counts to accommodate variable prompt lengths.
Avoid injecting load directly into customer pools; use dedicated sandbox pool with same hardware/instance profile and routing tags for acceptance runs.

Autoscaler policy under test will include a conservative and an aggressive profile; acceptance requires the conservative profile to meet SLOs for steady-state and the aggressive profile to handle step spikes without safety violations.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Li): request clearer customer-facing wording for acceptance criteria and a shorter playbook for Solutions Eng (ACTION: condense into 1-page checklist).
Design (Priya Rao): recommended dashboard presets for the acceptance run with pre-configured panels for violations and autoscaler timelines.
Security (Tomás Alvarez): flagged credential handling in replay-mode; mandated short-lived tokens and audit logging for any trace ingestion.
Infra (Lena Schmidt): suggested running calibration on at least two different GPU families to capture kernel scheduling variance.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal validation on sandbox pools (this ticket) — produce reproducible artifacts and calibration mapping.
Phase 2: Solutions piloting with two customers (AcmeChat and LedgerAI) using the acceptance script; collect signoffs.
Phase 3: bake into Dedicated onboarding checklist and add automated nightly calibration runs for fleet health.
Phase 4: add to production Certification pipeline as a gating check for Dedicated pool handoff.
